thread:
Leah Park: quick RFC follow-up — I'm proposing we decompose the intake surface into three small processes: validator (lightchecks + manifest verification), enqueuer (accepts artifacts and schedules bench jobs), and bench-adapter (runs heavy probes).
Ravi Singh: curious why 3 vs 2? what's the main perf / owner win?
Leah Park: splitting lets us: 1) keep fast path for light acceptance (sub-100ms) separate from long-running bench; 2) reduce blast radius when bench infra changes; 3) allow different scaling & SLA per component.
Tom B.: sounds good in theory. worried about duplicated state and cross-service contracts. how do we guarantee the validator's output is authoritative?
Priya N.: +1 on contracts concern. suggest a minimal protobuf manifest: {manifest_version: "v1", model_id, artifacts: [{path, sha256}], compat_level}. Keep it read-only in S3 and pass reference (s3://bucket/manifest.json).
Jules: also, bench workers need deterministic inputs for golden-set runs. we should pin a canonical manifest + seed vectors. otherwise bench diffs become noisy.
bench-bot: note: last bench run for model-x took 18m and blocked intake for 12 models in queue.
Ravi Singh: okay. what about latency for sync validators? do we accept async validation with fast-accept then veto later? that's risky for downstream consumers.
Leah Park: thinking phased: Phase 0 = no change, Phase 1 = extract validator as a sync filter that returns "accepted|rejected|accepted_pending_bench". Phase 2 = enqueuer takes accepted_pending_bench and a separate bench-adapter pool picks it up. Phase 3 = run canary rollouts where if bench fails we mark model as deactivated and notify owner.
Tom B.: fallback semantics need explicit design. if validator returns accepted_pending_bench, runtime should route to a safe model variant (fallback) until bench passes. otherwise product could serve unvetted model.
Priya N.: implement compatibility_level in manifest (e.g. "basic","strict","experimental"). runtime routing reads that and chooses fallback policy. also include schema: manifest.v1.json sha256.
Jules: for cross-service calls use gRPC with a small shim to keep protobuf shared. avoids json schema drift.
Ravi Singh: curious about telemetry and debug traces. how will we correlate intake events with bench runs? need a trace_id propagated across services.
Leah Park: yes—every intake request gets intake_id; enqueuer writes intake_id -> bench_job_id to consistent KV (Dynamo/Spanner). bench-adapter logs bench_job_id, bench metrics, pass/fail, and attaches commit sha + manifest sha.
Tom B.: cost tradeoff: benching everything costs $$$. propose sampling thresholds: full bench for production-intent models, lightweight fuzz for experimental. attach heuristics to "compat_level".
Priya N.: migration-wise, propose a compatibility shim: existing intake API continues to work; behind the scenes we route to new validator. if any regression, flip flag. rollout steps: 1) protobuf + shim, 2) validator split, 3) enqueuer extraction + bench pool split, 4) golden-set integration tests, 5) canary.
Ravi Singh: test plan? we need unit tests for validator, integration against a small golden set, and a perf test harness that simulates spikes. also add chaos tests for KV unavailability.
Leah Park: agreed. rough timeline: 2 weeks for proto & shim, 3 weeks for validator + tests, 4 weeks for enqueuer + bench adapter + perf tuning. we should aim small PRs and feature flags.
Jules: one more ask — add "lint" step to validator to normalize manifests (strip non-deterministic metadata) to avoid bench churn.
Tom B.: ops: who owns bench-adapter infra? bench team or runtime infra? need clear ownership or cross-team SLAs.
Priya N.: I'll tag bench infra and runtime leads in the RFC. also propose an off-ramp: if bench backlog grows above threshold use a cheaper approximate bench (quantized fastpass).
Leah Park: thanks all. action items: Priya to draft proto + manifest spec, Ravi to sketch telemetry KV model, Tom to outline fallback routing semantics, Jules to enumerate golden-set seed vectors. I'll assemble phased rollout doc and link back here. :raised_hands:
Ravi Singh: ack, I'll put a small example trace header in the proto: intake_id (uuid), parent_request_ts, source.
Priya N.: starting proto PR today, will ping for review. :sparkles:
bench-bot: reminder: please attach benchmark budget estimate when requesting bench pool capacity.
Leah Park: noted. will include budget and schedule in the RFC follow-up doc. :+1:
Tom B.: cool. one more micro-suggestion: add a "vetted_version" field in model registry so runtime can pick the last bench-passing version automatically.
Jules: lgtm. end-to-end smoke command for local dev: `./intake-smoke --manifest ./tests/fixtures/manifest.v1.json --trace-id $RANDOM`
Leah Park: perfect. closing thread once docs PRs exist. thanks everyone.
